title: Replicating the paper
text: grid follows paper’s sample (Section 1.2): treatment groups 24 34, event times 0 5, pre-treatment event times −4-4 −2-2 (baseline age d−1d - 1), control groups age 40. helper pre-treatment (validation) figures, one line per control group:
code: library(childpen) library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2) theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))  sim <- simulate_data(n_individuals = 30000, treatment_groups = 24:40) res <- multiple_treatment_group_analysis(sim, treatment_groups = 24:34,                                          periods_post = 5, periods_pre = 3,                                          max_control_group = 40, verbose = FALSE) pre_plot <- function(df) {   ggplot(df, aes(event_time, est, ymin = ci_l, ymax = ci_h,                  colour = factor(control_offset), fill = factor(control_offset))) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +     geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +     scale_x_continuous(breaks = -4:-2) +     labs(x = "Event time", y = "Estimate", colour = "Control offset", fill = "Control offset") }

title: Aggregate estimates across treatment groups — aggregate_estimands
text: results data.frame returned multiple_treatment_group_analysis, unmodified (attributes carry influence functions treatment-group sizes). weights weight treatment groups: "sample" (default): treatment-group shares. Within gender, \(w_{g,d} = n_{g,d} / \sum_{k} n_{g,k}\), DID_Female DID_Male; across genders, \(w_d = n_d / \sum_{k} n_{k}\), methods. "uniform" NULL: equal weight per treatment group. named numeric vector (names = treatment groups): fixed weights, renormalized sum one groups present event time. Groups missing vector get weight zero, warning. methods Methods aggregate (default: ). DID_Female, DID_Male: weighted_avg ratio_of_avgs theta; Conventional: weighted_avg gap_theta; NTD TD_E_LOGS: weighted_avg rho_effect accounting rows rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other; TD: weighted_avg gap_ATE; TD_PR: weighted_avg gap_theta_pre. include_pre Logical (default FALSE). Also aggregate pre-treatment event times. pre-treatment event time one cell per control group (control_offset = \(d' - d\)), offset aggregated separately, row validation test one treatment-control distance.

title: Aggregate estimates across treatment groups — aggregate_estimands

title: Aggregate estimates across treatment groups — aggregate_estimands
text: agg_type = "weighted_avg" \(\sum_d w_d B_d\) treatment-group estimates \(B_d\). DID_Female / DID_Male \(\theta_{Agg,1}(g, e)\); Conventional conventional aggregate gap \(\Delta\theta_{Agg}(e)\), NTD biased gap normalized effects (Theorem 1); NTD \(\rho_{Agg}(e)\), aggregate effect parenthood gender earnings ratio. agg_type = "ratio_of_avgs" (rows ) \(\theta_{Agg,2}(g, e)\), ratio weighted average ATE weighted average APO; puts weight higher-earning groups, paper prefers \(\theta_{Agg,1}\) (Section 5.1). Standard errors. influence function aggregate (aggregate estimator section appendix estimation inference) sums treatment-group influence functions weights; weights = "sample" adds term estimated shares, \(\psi_{(e)} = P_e^{-1}\sum_d [(B_d - (e))\psi_{p_d} + p_d\psi_{B_d}]\), \(\psi_{p_d} = 1\{D = d\} - p_d\), \(p_d\) share persons group \(d\) (\(1\{G = g, D = d\} - p_{g,d}\) joint share gender \(g\) group \(d\) within-gender rows) \(P_e\) summed share aggregated groups. ratio_of_avgs chain rule applied ratio two weighted averages, share term. Standard errors clustered person. share term put person-age scale average number ages per person, exact balanced panel. every treatment group estimate every event time; event time uses groups present, n_groups reports many.

text: Earnings person \(\) age first birth \(D_i\) age \(\) $$\log Y_{,} = h_{D_i}() + \kappa() F_i + \tau_{F_i}(D_i, - D_i)\,1\{\ge D_i\}   + \alpha_i + \varepsilon_{,},$$ \(F_i = 1\) women : Career entry growth (selection timing): \(h_D() = 9.6 + 0.02 (- 20) + \beta(D) x - 0.0015 x^2\), experience \(x = \max(- s(D), 0)\), entry age \(s(D) = 20 + 0.7 (D - 24)\) slope \(\beta(D) = 0.09 + 0.008 (D - 28)\). Later first births enter labor market later (schooling) grow faster. treatment, distant control groups yet working grow slowly, pre-treatment estimates grow magnitude distance control group negative distant control groups (closest ones small can positive); treatment, later control groups grow faster, parallel trends fails negative violation earlier treatment groups. Gender gap age: \(\kappa() = -0.04 - 0.015 \max(- 25, 0)\), female/male ratio absent children \(e^{\kappa()}\): 0.96 age 25, falling. Effects parenthood: mothers \(\tau_f(D, e) = -0.45 + 0.02 (D - 24) + 0.04 \min(e, 5)\) (smaller later first births, fading event time \(e\)); fathers \(\tau_m = -0.02\). normalized terms \(\theta(g) = e^{\tau_g} - 1\). Noise: \(\alpha_i \sim N(0, 0.20^2)\) (permanent), \(\varepsilon_{,} \sim N(0, 0.15^2)\) (transitory), independent everything else. Age first birth: drawn treatment_groups probabilities proportional normal density mean 29 standard deviation 4, independently gender. design -PT TD-PT fail; TD-E-LOGS holds exactly (gender terms cancel log means); NTD-PT TD-PR hold approximately, gender ratio changes age baseline target age.
